questions.question_text: A collection contains $430$ buttons. How many buttons are $10\%$ of the collection?

options.why: Subtracted $10$ from $430$ instead of dividing the quantity by $10$.
Divided by $100$, finding $1\%$ instead of $10\%$.
Used the percentage number as the answer without applying it to the collection.

questions.question_text: A recipe uses $520$ grams of oats. What mass is $25\%$ of the oats?

options.why: Halved the mass once, finding $50\%$ instead of halving again for $25\%$.
Divided by $10$, finding $10\%$ rather than $25\%$.
Subtracted $25$ from $520$ instead of finding one quarter of the mass.

questions.question_text: A length of cord is $34$ metres. What length is $50\%$ of the cord?

options.why: Doubled the length instead of halving it to find $50\%$.
Divided by $10$, finding $10\%$ rather than $50\%$.
Halved the digits separately, using half of $3$ as $1$ and half of $4$ as $2$.

questions.question_text: Which operation finds $25\%$ of a quantity?

options.why: Used the shortcut for $50\%$, which is one half, instead of the one quarter that matches $25\%$.
Recognised the quarter but reversed the operation, making the quantity four times larger instead of smaller.
Made both slips at once: read $25\%$ as one half and then multiplied instead of dividing.

questions.question_text: A ribbon is $7.8$ metres long. What length is $50\%$ of the ribbon?

options.why: Divided by $10$, finding $10\%$ of the length rather than $50\%$.
Doubled the ribbon length instead of halving it.
Halved the digits separately and treated half of $8$ tenths as $4$ tenths without regrouping $7$ wholes.

questions.question_text: Which is greater: $25\%$ of $240$ shells or $50\%$ of $130$ shells, and by how many?

options.why: Calculated $60$ and $65$ but reversed which result was greater.
Used the larger percentage amount itself instead of subtracting the two amounts.
Used the $25$ percentage-point gap as though it were the difference in shell counts.

questions.question_text: From an $80$ metre roll, $50\%$ is used for one project and $25\%$ for another. How much remains?

options.why: Added the used lengths and reported the amount used instead of the amount remaining.
Subtracted only the $50\%$ section and ignored the additional $25\%$ section.
Treated $50\%$ and $25\%$ as $50$ metres and $25$ metres, then subtracted $75$ from $80$.
